package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multiple layers of obfuscated JavaScript that, upon installation, initiates a chain of malicious actions: it fetches and executes additional malware from remote servers, exfiltrates sensitive data, and installs further payloads. It abuses npm lifecycle scripts (postinstall) to trigger these actions, employs anti-forensic techniques such as artifact deletion to evade detection, and leverages process spawning and in-memory payload loading to complicate analysis and detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the postinstall script executes install.js, which initiates a network request to download and execute further malicious payloads, resulting in the start of the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of the postinstall script to execute arbitrary code is a common malware technique, especially when the invoked script is obfuscated or fetches remote content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require network access or remote code execution during installation, and typically do not execute obfuscated scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall for setup or dependency checks, but not for downloading and executing remote code.
key_indicators: execution of external or obfuscated code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fetches a remote JavaScript payload from ipcheck.cloud, accumulates the response data, and executes it using eval, enabling dynamic delivery and execution of malicious code from an external server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code at runtime using eval is a hallmark of malware, as it allows attackers to deliver and execute arbitrary code after installation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute code from untrusted remote sources, especially not via eval.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin systems may fetch code, but with strict validation and never via direct eval of untrusted content.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the obfuscated JavaScript spawns a PowerShell process using Node.js child_process, passing an obfuscated command string to download, decrypt, and execute further payloads, escalating the attack chain and enabling cross-platform infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning PowerShell from Node.js is highly unusual and is often used for malicious purposes, especially when the command is obfuscated and used to download and execute further payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate JavaScript packages do not invoke PowerShell for arbitrary code execution or multi-stage payload delivery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate use; sometimes seen in cross-platform scripting for devops tools, but not with obfuscated or malicious intent.
key_indicators: multi-stage payload delivery via external scripts

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell script downloads a binary payload from mirotalk.net, decrypts it using XOR, and loads it as a DLL in memory via reflection, resulting in in-memory execution of malware without writing the DLL to disk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading, decrypting, and loading DLLs in-memory is a classic malware technique to evade disk-based detection and forensic analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts do not perform in-memory DLL loading from remote sources, nor do they decrypt and execute code in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate automation or red-team tools, but not in standard package scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After payload execution, the PowerShell script deletes the downloaded payload file from the temporary directory, removing forensic evidence and hindering post-infection analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Immediate deletion of artifacts after execution is an anti-forensic technique designed to hinder investigation and detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not erase their own payloads post-execution, except in rare cases such as self-cleaning installers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare, except in some self-cleaning installers or temporary file cleanup routines, but not for payloads.

attack_chain.action: Malicious postinstall script triggers execution of install.js during npm install.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote JavaScript payload.

attack_chain.action: install.js fetches and executes obfuscated JavaScript from a remote malicious domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of further malicious logic, including process spawning.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript spawns a PowerShell process to download and execute additional payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell script execution and payload delivery.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script downloads, decrypts, and loads a DLL payload in-memory.
PowerShell script deletes the downloaded payload to erase forensic evidence.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall script triggers network requests or executes obfuscated scripts
JavaScript code using eval on content fetched from remote domains
Node.js child_process spawning PowerShell with obfuscated or suspicious commands
PowerShell scripts downloading, decrypting, and loading DLLs in-memory
Immediate deletion of downloaded payload files after execution (anti-forensics)
file_indicators: package.json with suspicious postinstall scripts referencing install.js
scripts/install.js containing obfuscated code or network-fetching logic
Presence of temporary files in %TEMP% or /tmp/ related to payloads (e.g., payload.bin)
network_indicators: HTTP(S) requests to non-standard or suspicious domains during install or runtime
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that initiate network connections or execute obfuscated code. Flag any use of eval on remote content, especially from suspicious domains such as ipcheck.cloud or mirotalk.net. Detect Node.js processes spawning PowerShell or other shell interpreters with obfuscated commands. Watch for PowerShell scripts that download, decrypt, and load DLLs in-memory, and for immediate deletion of payload files after execution. Correlate these behaviors with known indicators of compromise (IoCs) and suspicious domains to identify malicious activity.
